title: HabitPact
summary: A private accountability app where friends set goals together, verify each other's progress, and put real stakes on follow-through — built to test whether habits stick better inside a trusted group than they do alone.
problem: Most habit trackers depend almost entirely on self-discipline: a streak counter and your own willpower. HabitPact explores a different bet — that follow-through gets stronger when the goal, the proof, the validation, and the consequence all live inside a friend group you don't want to let down. Users create a pact, commit to it, submit proof, and have peers approve it, with points-based stakes on the line.
approach: Owned the whole problem, not just the code — product concept, user journeys, product rules and edge cases, architecture, and release readiness, from whiteboard to a beta-ready build. Built cross-platform in Flutter on Firebase (Auth + Firestore + Cloud Functions), using AI-assisted development to move fast while independently validating the generated code, state behavior, persistence, and edge cases against real acceptance criteria rather than trusting it blindly.
outcome: Taken from concept to a beta-ready product: 167 automated host tests passing, tested on 2 physical Android devices, and a release APK produced. Built solo, 0-to-1 — a working, demoable cross-platform app with friend groups, proof submission, and peer validation functional in the prototype.
